patch.value: Outcome: every issue and pull request has at least one verified comment containing a live .agents/pm/issues/pm-*.toon link. Preserve existing comments and immutable artifact history. Use read-only census first, derive links from valid body PM IDs where possible, manually resolve the remaining no-ID or retired-ID artifacts, write at a conservative bounded rate, and re-census after each checkpoint. Never treat attempted writes as success. Record GitHub rate-limit receipts and exact remaining artifact numbers.
Historical GitHub artifact linkage: backfill canonical pm-item comments with resumable, rate-limit-aware evidence

Complete and continuously verify the repository-wide invariant that every GitHub issue and pull request has a public comment linking its canonical pm item. The 2026-08-04 audit found all 28 open issues compliant, then identified 468 historical closed artifacts without a PM-link comment before attempting a deterministic body-ID backfill. GitHub accepted a bounded subset and then returned a secondary content-creation rate limit; subsequent GraphQL census calls were intermittently unavailable with unexpected EOF. This item owns a resumable archive census, canonical-ID reconstruction for artifacts whose bodies contain no live PM ID, write pacing, verification, and a recurrence gate.

A read-only full census reports every GitHub issue and pull request and the exact comment-linked count.; Every artifact has a verified comment linking a live canonical pm item; ambiguous historical artifacts have documented manual mapping decisions.; Backfill is resumable and idempotent, uses conservative pacing, and never reports an attempted comment as successful without read-back.; A regression check detects newly created GitHub artifacts without a PM link comment.
The open backlog is compliant, but historical GitHub discussion still cannot reconstruct canonical PM lineage and bulk repair is constrained by GitHub secondary write throttling.

Read-back is required before the remaining count is trusted.
